body:
**Board organization above boards** · decided 2026-08-25, shipped 2026-08-26

**The answer: G + F, then E.**

- **G — Groups of boards** (rightmost frame) · explicit, coloured groups for areas of work — "Side pane", "Account page", "Brand" — each holding boards; boards keep their frames and screens as today. Agents get one optional `group` arg on `add_board`/`update_board`; group management lives in the canvas. **Shipped.**
- **F — Multiple design folders per repo** (row 2) · the project layer, which is where design tools generally put nesting. `velloo init` offers to create another; `velloo run` starts them all. **Shipped.**
- **E — Canvas regions** · the same idea one level down; the primitive is already in the schema. **Still open.**

**Not doing:** A as drawn (superseded by G, which is A's model with E's colour language) · **B** (retired — projects are answered by F) · **C**'s tags (pins + recency still worth taking on their own) · **D** (rejected: deriving groups from the name makes renaming silently refile a board).

Each frame's note carries the schema shape, agent surface and failure mode.

**A — Groups over the flat list**

A grouping layer *on top of* `boardOrder`. Boards stay a flat pool of files; a group is a label + an ordered id list, with collapsible headers and an implicit "Ungrouped" bucket for everything an agent just created.

- **Schema** — `config.boardGroups` next to `boardOrder`. Absent field = today's behaviour: zero migration.
- **MCP** — additive. An agent that ignores groups still works; its board lands in Ungrouped, visible, not lost.
- **UX** — create / rename / collapse / delete-group-keep-boards; drag between groups; top bar shows `Group / Board`.
- **Failure mode** — grouping is advisory, and a board sits in only one group. With 40 boards across 4 workstreams, groups get long and the sidebar still scrolls.
- **Cost** — smallest of the three.

**B — Projects (first-class, two levels)**

A project owns its boards, and the sidebar scopes to one project at a time — a 40-board folder shows six rows. The shape `velloo.json` already uses one level up.

- **Schema** — a real entity. Board ids need a scope (two projects will both want `landing`), which means **migration** for every multi-board folder plus a default "Main" project.
- **MCP** — not additive. Every agent prompt that says "list the boards" now has a hidden current project, and **a wrong-project board is invisible**, not just badly filed.
- **UX** — best at scale, worst at small scale: a 3-board folder pays a switcher for nothing, and a shared brand board has no clean home.
- **Failure mode** — hidden state. Agents have no selected project, so they need it passed every call or they all pile into the default.
- **Cost** — highest.

**C — Flat + facets (no hierarchy)**

Keep one list; make it navigable instead of nested: a filter box, tag chips with counts, a pinned section, recency sections. A board is found, not located.

- **Schema** — optional `tags` and `pinned` on the board. Fully additive, zero migration.
- **MCP** — agents can tag on creation from context without ever knowing a container exists — the model that best fits how agents work.
- **UX** — a board can carry several tags, which A and B both forbid. Pins keep the boards you're in at the top.
- **Failure mode** — no *shared* structure: tags drift (`brand`, `branding`), and 40 untagged boards degrade back to today's scroll. There's no "these five boards are one piece of work" object to hand to a teammate.
- **Cost** — low.

**Not exclusive** — C is the cheap floor under either A or B.

**D — Derived groups — REJECTED 2026-08-25**

The idea: group by name prefix — `Canvas — Settings dialog` collapses under a `Canvas` header, computed, never stored. It cost nothing and would have grouped 22 of 39 local boards on day one.

**Why it's out:** it breaks renaming. Under D a rename silently refiles the board — drop the prefix and it leaves its group; typo it and it forms a group of one. There's no way to change the name without the grouping, or the reverse. Cheap to build, expensive to live in.

Superseded by **G**: an explicit, coloured group, edited in the canvas, where renaming and refiling stay two different actions.

**E — Groups as canvas regions (the primitive that already exists)**

A common second answer in canvas tools: named, coloured regions of frames. `BoardGroup` (`{ id, name, color? }`) is already in the schema and frames carry the group id; what's missing is HTTP exposure and any canvas UI.

- **Region geometry is derived**, not stored — the tint is the bounding box of the member frames, so nothing can go stale.
- **The sidebar gets a second level for free.** Expand a board to list its regions; clicking one zooms to it. Hierarchy that maps to what you can see is the kind that lasts.
- **It doesn't fix the sidebar list.** Folders inflate by workstream, not by variant. E is why a variant set should never *become* three boards; workstreams that really are separate boards are G's problem.
- **Cost** — bigger than D, smaller than B.

**F — Multiple design folders per repo**

Decision taken 2026-08-25: a repo can hold several design folders, and `velloo init` on a repo that already has one should offer to create another. This is the layer where design tools generally put nesting.

**Most of it already exists.** `velloo.json` (shipped 2026-07-10) already names design folders as projects, and the CLI resolves a project name or a path.

**F1 — the init prompt.** Add "Create another design folder" as the first option, ask for a path and a project name, then run the normal wizard. Each folder registers its own MCP server.

**F2 — the canvas admits the other folders exist.** A folder chip in the top bar lists the repo's folders with their daemon state. Switching **navigates to that folder's own canvas** — no merging; every folder keeps its own daemon, history and theme.

With F shipped, "projects" is answered at the folder layer, which retires B.

**G — Groups of boards (the pick, 2026-08-25)**

A's data model with E's visual language. A group is an *area of work* — "Side pane", "Account page", "Brand" — holding boards; each board stays exactly what it is today.

- **Schema** — `config.boardGroups: [{ id, name, color? }]` plus `group?` on the board. No `group` = the implicit Ungrouped section, so no migration.
- **MCP** — no group CRUD tools. `add_board`/`update_board` take an optional `group`; naming a new one creates it. An agent can file a board it made, and can't otherwise reorganise the folder.
- **Canvas owns grouping** — create, rename, recolour, reorder, collapse, move boards, all in the sidebar.
- **Why not D** — a name prefix makes renaming silently refile the board. **Why not B** — projects are answered one level up by F.
- **Pairs with E** — regions group frames, groups group boards. Ship G first (it's the list that hurts), E after.
